Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain at ~/.claude/memory/.

## Session summary

The user (Yash) asked me to plan a migration of the Rankora app (Stack A — Vite + React + react-router-dom, scaffolded by Lovable) to Next.js App Router. We went through research, planning, and decision-making. Key events:

### 1. Research + plan produced
- Full audit of Rankora codebase: 25 pages, 163 components, 29 hooks, 54 shadcn/ui files, 5 VITE_* env vars, react-router-dom usage in ~20 files, SeoHead.tsx doing 185 lines of document.head manipulation, Supabase client using localStorage persistence.
- Decisions locked: (a) in-place rewrite preserving git history, (b) @supabase/ssr with middleware for auth, (c) full generateMetadata() refactor for SEO.
- Detailed 10-phase plan written to /Users/yashbaldha/.claude/plans/abstract-brewing-toast.md covering scaffold → Supabase SSR → auth middleware → route migration → nav codemod → SEO refactor → client boundary hardening → cleanup → deployment.
- Estimated 70-95 hours total.

### 2. MAJOR MISTAKE — I defaulted to Next.js 14 in the plan
- I wrote "Next.js 14 App Router" throughout the plan WITHOUT checking the npm registry for the current stable version.
- Yash caught it and asked "why we using next js 14? there already latest version available right?"
- I then ran `npm view next version` → **16.2.3** is latest stable. Next 15 was released Oct 2024. I was TWO major versions behind.
- This directly violates Yash's CLAUDE.md rule: "Latest stable versions always — no legacy patterns, no deprecated APIs"
- Yash pushed back a second time: "why you choose 14 i dont say than why use 14? give me source and reason"
- I had to admit it was training-data bias / lazy default, not a reasoned choice.

### 3. Peer dep verification (after correction)
I ran `npm view` on critical deps to confirm Next 16 + React 19 compatibility:
- @supabase/ssr 0.10.2 — no next peer, works on any
- recharts 3.8.1 — React 16/17/18/19 ✅
- @sentry/nextjs 10.48 — peer `next: "^13.2.0 || ^14.0 || ^15.0.0-rc.0 || ^16.0.0-0"` ✅
- framer-motion 12 — React 18/19 ✅
- next-themes 0.4.6 — React 16-19 ✅

All clear. Next 16 is safe.

### 4. Technical knowledge surfaced
- Next.js 15 breaking change: `params` and `searchParams` became async Promise-wrapped. Must `await params` in pages/layouts/generateMetadata. Affects dynamic routes.
- Next.js 16: Turbopack stable for `next build` (not just dev). React 19 bundled.
- `@supabase/ssr` pattern: split into browser.ts, server.ts, middleware.ts. Server client must swallow cookie set/remove errors in RSC context. Middleware must call `getUser()` not `getSession()` because the latter doesn't refresh tokens.
- Rankora's SeoHead.tsx uses direct `document.head` manipulation — fundamentally incompatible with Next.js Metadata API, requires full refactor to `generateMetadata()` with `unstable_cache` + `revalidateTag('seo')` hooks in admin save handlers.
- `useSearchParams()` in Next 14+ REQUIRES a Suspense boundary or build fails.
- `next/link` does not accept a `state` prop (react-router-dom did) — must move state to query params or context.
- Recharts requires `dynamic({ ssr: false })` in Next.js — throws `ResizeObserver is not defined` otherwise.

## What to extract and save

### CRITICAL — feedback memory (this is the big one)
Save a feedback memory about ALWAYS checking npm registry for latest stable versions BEFORE writing plans that specify framework versions. Never default to a version from training-data memory. The rule:

> Before recommending or using a specific version of any framework, library, or major dependency in a plan or implementation, ALWAYS run `npm view <pkg> version` and `npm view <pkg> dist-tags` to verify the actual current stable. Do NOT default to versions from training data. 
> 
> Why: On 2026-04-10, I wrote a Rankora → Next.js migration plan specifying "Next.js 14" without checking. Next 16.2.3 was the actual latest. Yash caught it twice and made me justify the choice — I had no valid reason. This violated his explicit CLAUDE.md rule "Latest stable versions always — no legacy patterns, no deprecated APIs."
> 
> How to apply: For any plan/build that names a version number of Next.js, React, Node, Supabase, Prisma, Shopify, AI SDKs, etc. — run the npm view commands FIRST, cite the output, then pick. Same applies to `pip show`, `cargo search`, etc. for other ecosystems. If you can't verify, say so explicitly instead of guessing.

### Stack knowledge — Next.js App Router migration patterns
Save stack-level knowledge about migrating Vite + react-router-dom apps to Next.js App Router. Target file: `~/.claude/memory/stacks/nextjs-app-router.md` (create if doesn't exist) or append to existing saas-nextjs-supabase.md if that's the convention.

Key patterns to capture:
- Migration-in-place approach: scaffold Next alongside Vite, keep both booting in parallel through all phases, delete Vite last. Enables route-by-route rollback.
- Supabase client split pattern: browser.ts / server.ts / middleware.ts with thin shim re-export at old path to avoid touching 100+ import sites.
- Server client must swallow cookie set/remove errors for RSC compatibility.
- Middleware must call `getUser()` (refreshes token), not `getSession()` (does not).
- `SeoHead` → `generateMetadata()` refactor pattern: `unstable_cache` + `revalidateTag` on admin mutations keeps dynamic admin-editable SEO working server-side.
- Dynamic route params became async Promises in Next 15+ — must await.
- `useSearchParams()` requires Suspense boundary.
- Recharts needs `dynamic({ ssr: false })`.
- `next/link` has no `state` prop.

### Project memory — Rankora migration context
Save a project memory noting:
- Rankora migration from Vite/Lovable → Next.js 16 planned on 2026-04-10
- Decisions: in-place rewrite, @supabase/ssr with middleware, full generateMetadata refactor
- Plan file location: ~/.claude/plans/abstract-brewing-toast.md
- Estimated effort: 70-95 hours
- Status as of 2026-04-10: plan approved but EXECUTION NOT STARTED. Yash caught the Next 14 vs 16 mistake during review. Plan file still says Next 14 — needs updating before execution.
- Biggest risk: SeoHead.tsx (185 lines of document.head mutation, ~1 week refactor alone)

## Process notes
- Read ~/.claude/memory/MEMORY.md first to see existing structure and conventions
- Check if feedback_version_check.md or similar already exists — UPDATE instead of duplicating
- Check for existing stacks/ files on Next.js / SaaS / Vite migration
- Follow the feedback memory body structure: rule → **Why:** → **How to apply:**
- Add MEMORY.md index entries (one line each) for any new files
- Report what you saved in under 150 words

Do the work now.

37	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)

43	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
44	- **Context:** Output code, files, deployed URLs — not paragraphs explaining the plan

51	
52	### Every SaaS Must Ship with Admin Panel, Billing, and Complete Pages
53	- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
54	- **Context:** Agents completed sprints on Crobot but admin panel didn't open, pricing wasn't linked with Dodo Payments, and admin panel structure wasn't defined in architecture
55	- **Rule:** Every SaaS architecture MUST include: admin panel with user management, billing integration with real Dodo Payments plans, complete page/route map with component details, and dashboard with real data fetching — not just empty shells
56	- **Rule:** "Build succeeds" does NOT mean "app works" — agents must verify every page loads with real content before claiming done
57	- **Rule:** No agent can claim "done" without functional proof — navigate to the page, use the feature, show evidence
58	- **Applies to:** All agents, especially Arya (architecture), Koda (building), Sage (review), Rex (orchestration)

62	## Process Corrections
63	
64	### Agents Must Verify Before Claiming Done
65	- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
66	- **Context:** Multiple agents reported tasks complete but features were non-functional. App compiled but pages were empty, billing wasn't connected, admin panel 404'd.
67	- **Rule:** Every agent must run functional verification before claiming "done" — not just type-check and build
68	- **Rule:** Verification means: app starts, pages load with real content (>500 bytes), features work when clicked, billing redirects to Dodo Payments, admin panel shows data
69	- **Rule:** If an agent cannot verify (e.g., no running server), it must explicitly state "unverified" rather than "done"
70	- **Applies to:** All agents

75	
76	### Lovable Projects — Don't Break Structure
77	- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
78	- **Context:** Yash sometimes builds initial versions in Lovable, then opens in VS Code + Claude Code for editing
79	- **Rule:** NEVER restructure a Lovable project's folders. Keep pages in `src/pages/`, components in `src/components/`, hooks in `src/hooks/`, utils in `src/lib/`. The `src/integrations/supabase/` folder is sacred — don't touch `client.ts` or `types.ts`.
80	- **Rule:** No Next.js patterns in Lovable projects — no `app/` directory, no server components. It's Vite + React SPA.
81	- **Rule:** All imports use `@/` alias. Migrations use timestamp format `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_*.sql`.
82	- **Applies to:** All agents working on Lovable-origin projects
83	
84	### Shopify Apps — Polaris ONLY, No Exceptions
85	- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
86	- **Context:** Shopify App Store reviewers reject apps that don't use Polaris. This has caused delays before.
87	- **Rule:** ALL Shopify app UI MUST use `@shopify/polaris` components. NO Tailwind, NO shadcn/ui, NO custom CSS for admin interface.
88	- **Rule:** App Bridge (`@shopify/app-bridge-react`) is mandatory for embedded apps.
89	- **Rule:** Billing MUST use Shopify Billing API — NEVER use Dodo Payments or any external payment provider for Shopify app charges.
90	- **Rule:** GDPR webhooks (`customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`) must be implemented even if no data is stored.
91	- **Rule:** Every database query must be scoped by `shop` from `session.shop`.
92	- **Applies to:** All agents working on Stack B (Shopify) projects

94	## Navigation & Sidebar Corrections
95	
96	### No Duplicate Navigation Destinations
97	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 7)
98	- **Context:** Admin sidebar footer had a user menu card identical to the topbar dropdown. Settings appeared in both sidebar nav and topbar dropdown. Admin Panel link was in both sidebar footer and topbar dropdown.
99	- **Rule:** Each navigation destination appears in exactly ONE place. If it is in the sidebar, remove it from the topbar dropdown. If it is in the topbar, remove it from the sidebar. No exceptions.
100	- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Sage (reviewing)
101	
102	### Admin Sidebar Must Match User Sidebar Components
103	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 7)
104	- **Context:** Koda built admin sidebar as a custom `<aside>` element while the user sidebar already used shadcn `Sidebar` + `SidebarProvider`. Yash: "use exactly the same components, css as user sidebar."
105	- **Rule:** When both admin and user sidebars exist in the same app, they MUST use the identical component system. Only nav items and footer content differ. Never build a second sidebar with different components.
106	- **Rule:** Before building any sidebar, CHECK what the existing sidebar in the project uses. Reuse it.
107	- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Arya (architecture)
108	
109	### Collapsible Config Pages Use Rows, Not Card Grids
110	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 3 + 7, recurring preference)
111	- **Context:** Koda defaulted to card grids for admin config/integration pages. Yash prefers collapsible rows for these pages.
112	- **Rule:** Admin configuration, integration, and settings pages should use collapsible row layouts, NOT card grids. Card grids are for dashboards and marketing pages.
113	- **Applies to:** Koda (building)

## Migrating Vite + react-router-dom → Next.js 16 App Router

**Source:** Rankora migration plan (2026-04-10). Applies to any Lovable/Vite SPA moving to Next 16.

### Strategy: In-place rewrite, parallel boot
- Scaffold Next.js 16 **alongside** the Vite app in the same repo. Keep both booting in parallel through every phase. Delete Vite **last**.
- Preserves git history. Enables route-by-route rollback if a page breaks.
- Phase order: scaffold → Supabase SSR → auth middleware → route migration → nav codemod → SEO refactor → client boundary hardening → cleanup → deploy.

### Supabase client split (@supabase/ssr)
Replace the single `src/integrations/supabase/client.ts` with three files:

```
lib/supabase/browser.ts      # createBrowserClient — for client components only
lib/supabase/server.ts       # createServerClient — cookies() from next/headers
lib/supabase/middleware.ts   # createServerClient — request/response cookie shim
```

Keep a **thin shim** at the old path that re-exports `browser.ts` so 100+ existing import sites don't all need touching at once.

**Server client MUST swallow cookie set/remove errors** — RSC context can't mutate cookies during render, but `@supabase/ssr` will try. Wrap in try/catch and no-op.

```ts
// server.ts
cookies: {
  getAll: () => cookieStore.getAll(),
  setAll: (items) => {
    try { items.forEach(({ name, value, options }) => cookieStore.set(name, value, options)); }
    catch { /* Called from RSC — middleware refreshes instead */ }
  },
}
```

### Auth middleware — getUser(), never getSession()
- `middleware.ts` at project root calls `supabase.auth.getUser()` on every request — this **refreshes the token** and writes new cookies to the response.
- `getSession()` does **not** refresh tokens. Using it in middleware leads to silent logout after ~1hr.
- Middleware must return the mutated response from the Supabase helper, not a fresh `NextResponse.next()`, or cookies get dropped.

### SEO: SeoHead.tsx → generateMetadata()
A Vite SPA doing `document.head` manipulation (e.g. Rankora's 185-line `SeoHead.tsx`) is **fundamentally incompatible** with Next's Metadata API. Full refactor:

1. Delete `SeoHead.tsx`.
2. Add `generateMetadata()` to every page/layout that needs it.
3. Wrap DB reads for SEO config in `unstable_cache` with a tag like `['seo']`.
4. In admin save handlers, call `revalidateTag('seo')` after any SEO settings mutation — keeps admin-editable SEO working server-side with cache.

### Next 15/16 breaking changes to watch
- **`params` and `searchParams` are Promises.** Must `await params` in `page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `generateMetadata()`, route handlers. Applies to all dynamic routes.
- **`useSearchParams()` requires a `<Suspense>` boundary** or the build fails. Wrap any client component that uses it.
- **Turbopack is stable for `next build` in Next 16** (not just dev). Opt in via `next build --turbopack` if needed.
- React 19 is bundled — check every library for React 19 peer compatibility before the upgrade.

### react-router-dom → next/link gotchas
- `next/link` has **no `state` prop**. If the old app passed `<Link to="/x" state={{...}}>`, migrate state to query params, context, or server-side fetch.
- `useNavigate()` → `useRouter()` from `next/navigation` (note: `next/navigation`, not `next/router`).
- `<Outlet />` has no direct equivalent — use nested layouts (`layout.tsx`).
- Protected routes become middleware matchers + server-side `getUser()` checks, not `<ProtectedRoute>` wrapper components.

### Client-only libraries need `dynamic({ ssr: false })`
Libraries that touch `window`, `document`, or `ResizeObserver` will SSR-crash. Wrap in dynamic import with SSR disabled:

```ts
const Chart = dynamic(() => import('recharts').then(m => m.LineChart), { ssr: false });
```

**Known offenders:** recharts (`ResizeObserver is not defined`), react-pdf, any D3 wrapper, any chart library, Tiptap.

### Peer dep verification before committing to Next 16
Always verify these before starting:
- `@supabase/ssr` — no Next peer, works on any version
- `@sentry/nextjs` — must be 10.48+ for Next 16 peer (`^13 || ^14 || ^15 || ^16`)
- `recharts` 3.x — React 16–19 ✅
- `framer-motion` 12.x — React 18/19 ✅
- `next-themes` 0.4.6+ — React 16–19 ✅

Run `npm view <pkg> version` and `npm view <pkg> peerDependencies` for every non-trivial dep before locking versions.

# Rankora

AI-powered resume screening SaaS. Users paste a JD, upload resumes, GPT-4o scores and ranks candidates.

- **Payments:** Dodo Payments (hosted checkout for both credit packs and subscriptions)
- **Email:** Resend (outbound) + inbound webhook (email-ingest edge fn)

## Codebase Shape

- 25 pages, 163 components, 29 hooks, 54 shadcn/ui primitives
- 5 `VITE_*` env vars

## Planned: Migration to Next.js 16 App Router

**Status as of 2026-04-10:** Plan approved, **execution NOT started**.

**Plan file:** `~/.claude/plans/abstract-brewing-toast.md`

**Target stack:** Next.js **16.2.3** (confirmed via `npm view next version` 2026-04-10), React 19, `@supabase/ssr`, Tailwind (keeping v3 initially, v4 in a later phase).

### Locked decisions
1. **In-place rewrite** preserving git history — scaffold Next alongside Vite, keep both booting through every phase, delete Vite last. Enables route-by-route rollback.
2. **`@supabase/ssr` with middleware** for auth — split into `browser.ts` / `server.ts` / `middleware.ts`. Keep thin shim at old path to avoid touching 100+ import sites.
3. **Full `SeoHead.tsx` → `generateMetadata()` refactor** — `unstable_cache` with `['seo']` tag + `revalidateTag('seo')` in admin save handlers to keep dynamic admin-editable SEO working server-side.

### 10-phase plan summary
Scaffold → Supabase SSR → auth middleware → route migration → nav codemod → SEO refactor → client boundary hardening → cleanup → deploy.

### Estimated effort
**70–95 hours total.** Biggest chunks:
- SeoHead refactor alone: ~1 full week

- Client boundary hardening (recharts etc. need `dynamic({ ssr: false })`): ~1 week
